column1: # FG-091 expected-suite manifest -- profile: harness
# WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT A COUNT. The bead is explicit: "a minimum script count
# is forbidden: it can false-green while required suites are missing." A count
# passes when the right number of the wrong suites run. This file names the
# exact set, and run_all --profile enforces SET EQUALITY against what discovery
# actually found: no missing, no unregistered, no renamed alias.
# OWNERSHIP IS DELIBERATELY INDEPENDENT OF DISCOVERY. run_all discovers whatever
# is executable under suites/; this file states what MUST be there. If those two
# disagree the profile fails, which is the entire point -- a suite that silently
# stopped being discovered, or one that appeared without being declared, is a
# change to the release surface and must be approved rather than absorbed.
# SCOPE OF THIS PROFILE, stated honestly: the three harness suites, which I own
# and can describe truthfully. It is NOT a release profile and does not claim to
# be. Other profiles belong to the owners of the suites they name; inventing
# owning-bead and proof-class values for fifty suites I do not own would be
# fabricated evidence, which is worse than a small true manifest.
# columns, tab-separated:
#   suite_id           the id run_all derives from the script path
#   owning_bead        the capability bead that owns the suite
#   gate               the gate/profile this entry belongs to
#   script_path        repository-relative path
#   targets            supported target classes, or "any"
#   classification     required | optional
#   proof_class        what a pass establishes, in claim-lattice terms
#   expected_terminal  the terminal status a pass must carry
